target: Macetnya parah banget tadi pagi di jalan ke kantor.
english: The traffic was really terrible this morning on the way to the office.
tip: Banget = sekali/sangat: parah banget = parah sekali (really bad). Spoken only.

target: Kue buatan nenek enak banget, aku makan tiga potong.
english: Grandma's homemade cake is so good, I ate three slices.
tip: Enak banget = enak sekali (so tasty). Banget follows the adjective.

target: Gimana kabar orang tuamu di kampung?
english: How are your parents doing back in the village?
tip: Gimana = bagaimana (how): gimana kabar…? = bagaimana kabar…?

target: Gimana kalau kita berangkat lebih pagi supaya tidak kena macet?
english: How about we leave earlier so we don't get stuck in traffic?
tip: Gimana kalau…? = bagaimana kalau…? ('how about…?'). Spoken form.

target: Jangan bicara gitu ke adikmu, nanti dia sedih.
english: Don't talk like that to your little sibling, you'll make her sad.
tip: Gitu = begitu (like that): bicara gitu = bicara begitu.

target: Kalau gitu, kita ketemu langsung di restoran jam delapan.
english: In that case, let's just meet at the restaurant at eight.
tip: Kalau gitu = kalau begitu ('in that case'). Spoken shortening.

target: Caranya gini: tekan tombol hijau, lalu pilih bahasa.
english: Here's how: press the green button, then choose a language.
tip: Gini opens explanations: caranya gini = 'here's how'. Spoken begini.

target: Dia memang suka bercanda gitu, jangan tersinggung.
english: He just likes to joke around like that, don't take offense.
tip: Sentence-final gitu ≈ 'like that, you know'. Spoken begitu.

target: Suaranya kayak penyanyi terkenal, padahal dia cuma karyawan biasa.
english: His voice is like a famous singer's, even though he's just a regular employee.
tip: Kayak = seperti (like): kayak penyanyi = seperti penyanyi.

target: Langitnya gelap, kayaknya sebentar lagi hujan deras.
english: The sky's dark; looks like it's going to pour any minute.
tip: Kayaknya = 'looks like/seems': kayaknya hujan = sepertinya hujan.

target: Kamu lagi ngapain di dapur malam-malam begini?
english: What are you doing in the kitchen this late at night?
tip: Ngapain = spoken 'doing what?': lagi ngapain? = sedang apa?

target: Ngapain kamu bawa payung? Di luar cerah begini.
english: Why'd you bring an umbrella? It's perfectly sunny out.
tip: Ngapain + verb = 'why bother': ngapain bawa payung? = why bring an umbrella?

target: Bantu aku angkat kardus ini dong, berat sekali.
english: Come on, help me lift this box, it's really heavy.
tip: Dong softens requests: bantu dong = 'come on, help me'. Spoken only.

target: Coba deh makan di warung sate dekat stasiun itu.
english: Go on, try eating at that satay stall near the station.
tip: Deh nudges a suggestion: coba deh = 'go on, try it'.

target: Besok aku ganti uangmu, janji deh.
english: I'll pay you back tomorrow — I promise, really.
tip: Sentence-final deh = 'really/I mean it': janji deh = I promise.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, aku berangkat sendiri deh.
english: If you're busy, fine, I'll just head out on my own then.
tip: Deh marks giving in: aku sendiri deh = 'fine, I'll go alone then'.

target: Kok kamu belum siap? Kita harus berangkat sekarang.
english: How come you're not ready yet? We have to leave now.
tip: Kok opens surprised questions: kok belum siap? = how come you're not ready?

target: Tenang, obatnya tidak pahit kok, anak kecil juga mau.
english: Don't worry, the medicine isn't bitter, really — even little kids take it.
tip: Sentence-final kok reassures: tidak pahit kok = 'it's not bitter, really'.

target: Kamu ini kenapa sih, dari tadi diam terus?
english: What is it with you, you've been silent this whole time?
tip: Sih sharpens a question: kenapa sih? = 'what IS it with you?'

target: Enak sih, tapi porsinya kecil untuk harga segitu.
english: It IS tasty, sure, but the portion is small for that price.
tip: Sih concedes before a 'but': enak sih, tapi… = it IS tasty, but…

target: Entar sore aku mampir ke rumahmu bawa oleh-oleh.
english: Later this afternoon I'll drop by your place with some souvenirs.
tip: Entar = nanti (later): entar sore = nanti sore.

target: Ntar dulu, aku masih cari kunci motor di tas.
english: Hold on a sec, I'm still looking for the motorbike key in my bag.
tip: Ntar dulu = nanti dulu ('hold on a sec'). Ntar/entar = spoken nanti.

target: Dia emang jago masak, semua tamu minta tambah.
english: He really is a great cook — all the guests asked for seconds.
tip: Emang = memang (really/indeed): emang jago = memang jago.

target: Emang kamu yakin tokonya buka hari libur begini?
english: Are you really sure the shop is open on a holiday like this?
tip: Question-opening emang = memang: 'is it really true that…?'

target: Aku ke bioskop sama teman kantor habis pulang kerja.
english: I went to the movies with some coworkers after getting off work.
tip: Spoken sama = dengan (with): sama teman = dengan teman.

target: Aku setuju sama pendapatmu soal jadwal baru itu.
english: I agree with your take on that new schedule.
tip: After verbs, sama = dengan: setuju sama = setuju dengan (agree with).

target: Teman saya di Jakarta bilang, "Gue tunggu lo di depan halte."
english: My friend in Jakarta said, "I'll wait for you in front of the bus stop." (street-casual)
tip: Jakarta slang pronouns: gue = saya, lo = kamu. Heard constantly; never use with elders.

target: Yuk berangkat sekarang, soalnya jalanan mulai ramai.
english: Come on, let's head out now, because the roads are getting busy.
tip: Yuk invites: yuk berangkat = 'come on, let's go'. Softer cousin of ayo.

target: Kamu bawa payung kan? Langitnya mendung dari tadi.
english: You brought an umbrella, right? The sky's been overcast for a while.
tip: Tag kan seeks agreement: bawa kan? = 'you brought it, right?'

target: Nih, aku bawakan mangga dari kebun tetangga.
english: Here, I brought you some mangoes from the neighbor's garden.
tip: Nih presents something at hand: nih = 'here (you go)'.
